newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks ends flat, OTCs dominate actives.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks ends flat, OTCs dominate actives.

text.p: Singapore shares ended flat on Thursday with retail interest focused on small-capitalised stocks and institutions buying selected blue chips.
Foreign funds were mostly lured into the Hong Kong bourse, which rallied into record highs on Thursday, dealers said.
"The focus is on regional funds, not so much the Singapore dollar stocks," said a dealer.
"The Singapore dollar stocks are relatively steady, providing little speculative opportunity," said another dealer.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended off by 0.79 point at 2,220.36 after trading within a narrow 10-point range.
Malaysian shares traded over-the-counter (OTC) such as MBf Holdings and Berjaya Group hogged the actives with over 19 million and 18 million shares respectively.
Precision engineering specialist Armstrong Industrial saw continued buying on better earnings prospects. The shares rose Singapore $0.07 (US$0.05) to S$0.675 on 15.7 million shares.
Foreign tranches of banks, like OUB and DBS led gainers on optimism over their prospects.
Total volume was 247.14 million shares with gainers outpacing losers by 222 to 144.
